Judaism and the Sins of Israel: On the Essential Nature of Religion
Israel, an "artificial state" established by Zionists, has brought immense catastrophe to Palestine and the Middle East, exerting a profound and unsettling impact on the global order while severely jeopardizing humanity's faith in justice. To enable a clearer discernment of the true nature of Judaism and the state of Israel, distinguish right from wrong, and offer humanity a glimmer of hope to rectify deviations and restore justice, this article systematically delineates their multiple transgressions.
1. Blaspheming God and Serving the Devil
Does God exist? It is a question to which no definitive empirical answer can be given. Yet, for any religion, the existence of God is an absolute certainty—a Supreme Being who created the universe and will ultimately deliver it. Since God created the world, the Divine must be inherently grand, righteous, and impeccable. God cannot behave like an earthly despot who blurs the line between right and wrong, harbors blind favoritism, or instigates conflict that leaves the earth devastated and drenched in blood. Any entity that perpetuates such horrors must be the devil, not God. God would deem it beneath Divine dignity to broker arbitrary covenants, grant exclusive real estate titles to specific mortals, demonstrate absolute partiality toward a selective few, or engage in physical wrestling matches with humans—much like a human would never engage in such absurdities with an ant, and would find it reviling to hear an ant boast of such a relationship. Therefore, what Judaism worships is the devil, not God; consequently, Judaism itself is the true object of divine retribution.
2. A Total Syndicate Snuffing Out the Beacon of Humanity
The ultimate purpose of religion is self-interest, utilizing individual benefit as a mechanism to attract adherents. This self-interest can be bifurcated into two categories: temporal self-interest in the material world, and transcendental self-interest in the afterlife. While the vast majority of religions pursue the latter, the modalities of religious dissemination can be categorized into three paradigms: self-interest, altruism, and self-abnegation.
· Righteous Religions: Expand their doctrines through structural altruism to attain both temporal and transcendental self-interest (modern Protestantism, to a qualified extent, approaches this paradigm).
· Neutral Religions: Enjoin strict self-abnegation to achieve transcendental self-interest (authentic Chinese Mahayana Buddhism emphasizes high self-abnegation and moderate altruism; Tibetan Buddhism, however, deviates from this).
· Malevolent Religions: Disseminate their faith via raw self-interest to maximize both temporal and transcendental gains (Judaism fits this mold).
· Criminal Syndicates: When a group systematically inflicts harm upon external populations to secure transcendental self-interest, it ceases to be a religion and becomes a criminal enterprise (such as ISIS).
True righteous religion is singular; it must rely on altruism as its proselytizing engine to fulfill its dual self-interest. Judged by this criterion, Islam must also be categorized as a cultish entity.
When a religion becomes pathologically insular yet fiercely unified for collective self-enrichment, it must perpetually extract illicit advantages from the external world to fulfill its internal theological promises and suppress external criticism or interference. This manifests through predatory usury, monopolistic syndicates, the systematic deprivation of opportunities for outsiders, the monopolization of media to strangle freedom of speech, the utilization of ill-gotten wealth to manipulate foreign governments, and the deployment of collective intimidation against dissenters. Judged by any objective metric, this exhibits the classic hallmarks of a mafia.
Consider the contemporary world: we witness the collective intimidation of protesting students at Harvard, where syndicates coerced the university administration to surrender blacklists and threatened a total hiring boycott against student dissidents. Even in my own experience, when attempting to publish a critique of Israel, editors at major media outlets felt compelled to cautiously warn me to "ensure my personal safety." These multi-faceted realities reveal a chilling truth: when confronting Israel, the constitutional right to free speech is immediately compromised by physical and professional security anxieties.
Look at the sheer absurdity of our global reality: within the United States—the very nation that birthed the United Nations and once stood as a beacon of civilization—the government stands in obstinate, isolated solidarity with Israel, defiantly opposing the overwhelming majority of the international community on Palestinian sovereignty. Nearly all mainstream political figures line up in lockstep behind Israel, even when the comment sections beneath their public statements are flooded with denunciation from the populace. Are we to believe that every single American politician is a fundamentally malicious actor? Facing the spilled blood of the Palestinian people and the living hell of their homeland, have these politicians truly been possessed by demons to consciously walk in alignment with evil? No matter how compromised these politicians may be, it is impossible that this reflects the genuine, uncoerced intent of all of them. This unveils a profoundly horrifying reality upon closer reflection: the United States is rapidly transforming into a hollowed-out zombie, its sovereign soul thoroughly extracted by Israel and Zionist interest groups.
3. Bloodlust Masked by Hypocritical Dogma
We must remain hyper-vigilant against a common tactic employed by certain theologians and scholars who attempt to sanitize Judaism by citing altruistic laws within its scriptures—such as the Decalogue, commands to "give alms to the poor," or prohibitions against "oppressing the stranger." However, any insular, predatory interest group must inevitably weave a cloak of righteous justice to survive within secular society and deflect external scrutiny. As the ancient proverb goes, "there is honor even among thieves"—the most ruthless cartels in history eagerly built bridges and paved roads for their local neighborhoods, and the most extreme cults frequently used charitable handouts to buy public compliance.
These manicured facades are by no means the essence of the system; they are merely moral ornaments designed to deceive the world. In practice, "giving alms to the poor" stands in irreconcilable, parasitic contradiction with "predatory usury and capital monopoly." Through usurious practices and financial blood-sucking, they drive millions of Gentile families into destitution and ruin; then, they turn inward to distribute welfare within their enclosed circle, placating their own kin and delivering on the material benefits promised upon initiation. This closed-loop mechanism of "extreme external predation coupled with internal distribution of spoils" precisely validates its absolute identity as a mafia syndicate. To evaluate an entity, one must look past its ornamental garments and examine whose fundamental right to survival it has stripped away. Any appeasement of this profound hypocrisy constitutes an outright betrayal of human justice.
4. Actions Divorced from Modern Civilization
The foundational premise of modern civilization dictating that the Earth is the shared home of all living things; even apex species possess no arbitrary right to violently displace or dispossess other creatures of their habitats. If humanity lacks the ethical authority to evict monkeys from a mountain to claim it for ourselves, who under heaven possesses the right to strip the Palestinian people of their sovereign right to exist and reside in Palestine?
Following the conclusion of World War II in 1945, Jewish populations no longer faced an existential threat to their survival; what, then, justified their subsequent threat to the very survival of the Palestinians? Apologists might argue that the Jewish community, having just endured the horrors of the Holocaust, was trapped in an extreme crisis of survival. Yet, this can never serve as a legitimate pretext for violent dispossession. Existential crises are not unique to the Jewish experience. According to the most basic threshold of fairness and justice in modern civilization, any localized catastrophe or crisis must be resolved at its historical source; it can never grant a right to displace the catastrophe onto innocent third parties by plundering their legitimate right to life. The bitter fruits of European anti-Semitism ought to have been borne by Europe itself. Forcing the native inhabitants of Palestine—who played absolutely no part in European crimes—to foot the bill for "moral reparations" of the Holocaust, and framing the so-called "two-state solution" as justice, represents one of the most hypocritical, shameless, and predatory acts of banditry in the history of modern international politics.
5. The Abuse of Violence to Perpetrate Genocide
For nearly eighty years, Zionist forces in Palestine have systematically displaced the indigenous population, brutally massacred and incarcerated Palestinians, and relentlessly expanded illegal settlements. This has triggered an endless exodus of refugees, resulted in innumerable casualties, and caused harrowing atrocities to play out on a daily basis—all driven by a calculated attempt to gradually liquidate the Palestinian people and completely usurp their land.
Thanks to the ubiquity of modern digital media, the tragic plight of the Palestinians is now laid bare before the collective conscience of humanity. Who, then, is the true terrorist? The moral framework governing the justifiable use of violence dictating that violence is righteous only when one's own survival or the survival of others is actively threatened. Consequently, the Palestinian people possess an absolute, legitimate right to employ violence against their Israeli oppressors. Their resistance is fundamentally just, whereas Israel constitutes the actual terrorist entity.
6. Constructing an Invisible Empire Parasitic Upon Modern States
By tightly binding religious identity to material self-interest, the Zionist cartel has engineered an invisible empire that effectively reigns supreme over sovereign nations. Leveraging their monopolized financial wealth and sprawling media conglomerates, they exert deep, manipulative control over Western political landscapes. This insular, self-serving apparatus utilizes aggressive financial lobbying to transmute the hard-earned tax dollars of foreign citizens into their own political leverage, ultimately hijacking the foreign policies of major global powers. This is a textbook case of a predatory interest group subverting, hollow out, and invisibly parasitizing modern democracy and sovereign civilization.
7. Ideological Thought Policing and the Destruction of Public Justice
To immunize themselves against external critique, these groups weaponize historical trauma, swiftly branding any discourse that interrogates their atrocities with the label of "anti-Semitism." This calculated form of ideological thought policing is brutally suffocating academic freedom and liberty of expression. As the world witnesses the blood-soaked purgatory inflicted upon the Palestinian people, Western politicians—paralyzed by the intimidation of powerful lobby groups—lapse into a collective, spineless silence, willfully aligning themselves with demonic forces. This absolute double standard has triggered a profound crisis of trust in modern morality, fundamentally dismantling humanity's self-evident faith in equity, justice, and universal law.

Despite the reality that certain factions within the Jewish populace remain bound by a nexus of religion and self-interest—forming an invisible, crushing force capable of flattening any individual resistance to suppress anti-Zionist critiques—there are still courageous Jewish individuals who actively resist Israeli policies and oppose draconian anti-Semitism legislation. Though born into the fold of Judaism, their conscience and commitment to justice have triumphed over institutional evil. They represent the true pride of the Jewish people and the sole beacon of hope for their eventual moral redemption.

Brian Stelter is upset that Politico wasn’t allowed on Air Force One on Monday. He shouldn’t be. A plane seat isn’t a right, and Politico spent years using that seat to promote one party.

The White House kept Politico off the plane for Trump’s trip to Nebraska. Politico was the assigned print pooler, the one reporter who files notes the rest of the print outlets share. Other outlets were offered the seat and declined it, so the trip had no primary print pooler. The Washington Post still flew as the secondary, and the TV pool was still on board.

Trump was right to start this fight. He pulled the White House passes of Politico, CNN, and MS NOW because those outlets spent years promoting one party. A judge ordered the building access restored. The administration says that order doesn’t cover the plane, and CNN has already been kept off it on its own pool days.

Biden never had to do this because the press pool was already on his side. The press buried the laptop story, falsely called Biden’s border secure, and kept his decline off the front page until a debate made it impossible.

Stelter isn’t actually mourning a missing reporter from Air Force One. He’s mourning a guaranteed seat for an outlet that spent years using it against one party and not the other.

I’m thankful that President Trump keeps calling out the activist media and reprimanding them. He’s doing all Americans a service with this, even those who don’t like him.

text:
🚀 Stock Study: Krishna Defence & Allied Industries Ltd (NSE: KRISHNADEF) ⚓🇮🇳

A niche, high-ROCE "picks & shovels" play on India's booming naval upcycle!

📊 Latest Snapshot (As of Oct 5, 2026):
• Share Price: ₹1,201.00
• Market Cap: ₹1,795 Cr
• P/E Ratio: 43.8x
• ROCE / ROE: 31.1% / 23.7%
• Debt-to-Equity: 0.01

🏢 The Business & Moat:
KDAIL is a Tier-1 metallurgical supplier to the Ministry of Defence, manufacturing critical shipbuilding steel sections (bulb bars), super alloy weld consumables, and T-90 tank chassis components. It operates as a monopoly or duopoly for several niche naval applications, protected by immense entry barriers including 10-year DRDO Tech Transfers and grueling 3-5 year naval quality approval cycles.

💰 Growth & Cash Flow Turnaround
FY26 was a fundamental breakout year. Net Profit (PAT) surged ~85% YoY to ₹38.12 Cr on revenues of ₹244.78 Cr. More importantly, the company historically suffered from long working capital cycles but successfully flipped this to generate a massive ₹86.05 Cr in Operating Cash Flow in FY26. The balance sheet remains highly unleveraged.

📈 Key Catalysts & Triggers

1️⃣ Unmanned Platforms: Currently constructing "Jalkapi," India's largest Extra-Large Unmanned Underwater Vehicle (XLUUV), which could elevate the company to a prime defense platform integrator.

2️⃣ Order Execution: Secured direct MoD orders, successfully bypassing shipyard intermediaries for better payment visibility.

3️⃣ Margin Support: Formalized an MoU under the Ministry of Steel's PLI 1.2 Scheme, which offers direct cash incentives on incremental production.

4️⃣ Institutional Visibility: Successfully migrated from the NSE SME Emerge platform to the NSE Mainboard.

⚠️ Key Risks

• High Working Capital: Naval supply chains are notoriously slow, leading to heavily extended inventory holding days.

• Customer Concentration: Over 90% of revenue is tied directly to the sovereign defense sector and shipyards.

• Commodity Risks: Fixed-price MoD contracts lack automatic pass-through clauses, leaving margins vulnerable to sudden raw material (specialty steel) inflation.

⚖️ Valuation Verdict
While broader defense peers (systems integrators and space tech) are trading at frothy 80x to 100x+ multiples, KDAIL trades at a comparatively reasonable 43.8x P/E. Given its >80% profit CAGR and >30% ROCE, it stands out as a compelling Growth-at-a-Reasonable-Price (GARP) candidate for aggressive investors backing the 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' defense theme.

For those unfamiliar with the story, here's the VERY basic version from Brent Friedman's (@BFree63 - BF) viewpoint. FYI, BF is the co-creator of "Dark Skies" with @BryceZabel).

~

In 1981, when BF was 18, his former neighbor, John Herrington (JH), who BF saw as a father figure, offered him some money and asked BF to drive his two cars, and the family dog from San Francisco to Virginia. JH was relocating to the DC area for work in the Reagan administration and would go on to become the Assistant Secretary of the Navy, and later, Secretary of Energy.

BF and his two friends made the cross-country trip and wound up at Herrington's house, with Friedman having a private conversation with his former neighbor.

JH told him he had been briefed in an underground facility for weeks for his new job, and cried himself to sleep every night. He also said, "aliens are real, they're here, and I've seen them." JH said the part of the briefing about aliens was on Day 3.

~From Sound, Light & Frequency~

Friedman: "I think that when people ask me, you know, 'You're a writer, how do we know that you didn't come up with this?' Well, it's laced with details I just could not have invented. It's beyond my capabilities. I'm just not that good of a writer. 

"Let me conclude how the whole story, essentially, ended. Which was, I said [to Herrington], 'My mind is reeling, and what I don't understand is you've told me all of this, and how do you know I'm not gonna go tell people myself about this?' And he said, 'Oh, I'm sure you will. But the question is, who's gonna believe you?'

"That kind of hit me in the solar plexus, like, wow, you're right [laughs]. Who is gonna believe an 18-year-old kid who's going off to UCLA to be a theater major? 

"Secondarily, he said, 'If you tell this story and you use my name, I'll just deny it, because that's how the cover-up works.'

"And so there I was with this incredible story, and already realizing there was no value to it, in terms of me telling anyone and being the whistleblower, right? If that was even crossing my mind. 

"But I have to say that, at 18 years old, I remember we'd stayed up late enough talking, and by the time I got downstairs where my friends were asleep down in the Rumpus room (a room usually in the basement of a home that is used for games, parties, and recreation), I remember laying there on my sleeping bag on the floor, looking up at this window and seeing the stars. And I thought, my whole world has just been turned upside down, and I don't think I fully understood how to process it. 

"But, I told that story to my family when I got back home, and I don't think I told it again until probably close to 30, when I was 30, because even my family had trouble believing it."

~

For the September 17th edition of @SchreckReports's "Signs of Life," he tracked down JH via email, spoke on the phone, and asked him about JF's claims. 

A summary...

Herrington: Brent who? I've never met him.

Schreckinger: Let me tell you his story and see if that refreshes your memory. 

Herrington: Oh yeah, I think he was a neighbor of mine. I DID pay for my car to be driven across the country but Friedman had nothing to do with that. It was my son-in-law who drove it. 

I didn't cry when briefed about UFOs and aliens, but I'm intrigued by those reports of Navy encounters with UAP. 

Friedman: I stand by my story. 

~

"And some people in the community have pointed out, 'Well, his daughters were in like, high school, middle school at this time.' So I interpret this as somebody who went on to be his son-in-law. I actually am looking into that a bit.

text: I shall tell a story to illustrate since intraconference play offers inconclusive results depending on timeframe measured, rankings at time of competition, and post season play including bowl games outside of the BCS. National championships in the BCS and CFP era tilt towards the SEC, but Alabama’s six chips loom large in that calculus. Remove Alabama and the results among remaining teams and conferences are comparable. The game day mythos surrounding Saturday football in the South builds a romanticized narrative that is hard to penetrate with facts. To argue with the diehard SEC fan is to accept the argument will eventually turn theological rather than a rational exploration of how we arrived at this moment of contention where the non SEC football world concurs in the bias shown to the SEC. Until expansion the SEC was generally understood to be dominated by a handful of teams rotating at the top and indistinguishable second tier teams.  Same with the B10, ACC and PAC 12. The Big12 only recently became something other than backyard offensive football with no defense. In the CFP era it became important to tout strength of schedule and quality losses as distinguishing criteria, devaluing conference championships. Saban was among the first to harp continuously about how hard SEC road games were regardless of the level of competition. At stake were limited playoff opportunities and huge paydays. Enter NIL and the upward pressure on player payments legitimizing the pay for play system long suspected to fuel top program success, particularly in the SEC. Players and coaches followed money which flows more free in the SEC than elsewhere because of rabid and desperate fan bases tired of being SEC doormats. Enter ESPN’s broadcast deal with both the SEC and the CFP which introduces the dynamic of conference preference and revenue driven match ups. Revenue driven match ups depend on relative rankings which rely heavily on preseason polling. Once competition begins there are significant barriers to movement into or out of the polls except in cases of egregious loss or unprecedented success.  This is called confirmation bias. Aided by a network incentivized to favorably promote the SEC, opinions are influenced towards its relative strength compared to conferences not subsidized in the same way. The last AP Top 25 stands as the most recent example of media created confirmation bias in action. At this point, with a 9 game schedule, the SEC is insulated from challenge except on the margins. Their remaining solution is to expand the CFP and allow for more intraconference match ups among the best teams in each P4 conference.

text:
The labor theory of value believes that value (which is what people pay for) is created by the labor done to produce the good or service on offer. It's preposterously easy to see how false it is. (What an embarrassment to Oren Cass!)est is:

"'Extra pay' is something you demand for doing work."

Okay, kids, that's called the "labor theory of value," and it's Marxist economic thinking. I recommend not listening to people who have used Marx's central conceptions as the foundations of their economic musings.

The labor theory of value believes that value (which is what people pay for) is created by the labor done to produce the good or service on offer. It's preposterously easy to see how false it is. (What an embarassment to Oren Cass!)

Here's an example!

One time, we needed a handyman to do some work for us, so we hired a guy we knew who needed the work. The thing is, the guy and his company had a quasi-mystical belief that work done without any power tools had a higher quality to it because it was done by hand instead of by machine. This probably would have been fine if he charged competitively by the job, but he didn't. He charged, in part, by the hour.

His work was insanely slower than it would have been with power tools and nail guns, so it turned out to be really expensive. It also wasn't done nearly as well as it might have been. The value created was lower, and the cost was higher, specifically because it took more labor. Labor ("extra work") did not create value here.

Here's another example!

Some people put a lot of labor into drawing useless pictures of anime fantasies or fan art or whatever. They're essentially worthless, but they take a lot of labor to produce between skills development and doing a good job. These things do not produce much value, though, even though they take considerable labor.

Labor is not the producer of value. Labor might be required to end up with value, but it isn't where value comes from. (In logic, we would call it a necessary but insufficient condition.)

Here's another example the other way!

It is entirely possible, if you live in the right place, to essentially dig a small hole in your yard taking less than ten minutes and find a diamond worth a million dollars (as was just found in Arkansas recently, apparently). Lots of value was produced with very little labor. You digging a little hole in your yard resulted in, but did not produce, a million dollars in value.

On the other hand, it's a lot more likely that you could go break your body digging in your yard for 15 hours a day until you're haggard and never find anything worth a dime. Lots of labor, same activity, no value.

The labor theory of value is stupid.

Actually, it's not just stupid; it's resentful.

The labor theory of value is the notion of a resentful person who thinks his work is intrinsically more valuable than it is and who resents that he isn't getting more for it than he is, either from the market or from an employer who is paying him to do things he probably couldn't do productively outside of that employment.

In my opinion, which isn't the opinion of a "Chief Economist" at a postliberal retard outlet, value is produced by solving problems for other people, which they are willing to pay for. Labor is a necessary condition to the production of that solution, but it isn't sufficient to determine the value produced because the value is determined otherwise: by how much solving a particular problem is worth to a person who needs it solved (because they can't solve it some other way, including through another service provider who does it more cheaply).

Anyway, Cass's failure to understand interest, by his own indication, seems to be a consequence of his having adopted Marx's resentful and wrong labor theory of value. To this I say, what a surprise!!

PS: Marx equipped his doctrine of the labor theory of value with a second crackpot belief that is relevant here too: the concept of "surplus value."

Marx believed the value in a product or service is produced by the labor which is only partially compensated for the value it produced. The owner (the capitalist) pockets the "surplus value" generated by the labor but not compensated by the wages he'll pay for that labor. Thus, the owner (capitalist) is exploiting the worker by extracting value from him that he doesn't pay. (Marx painted the picture for the worker more grimly than this, but we shan't digress.)

This is the same kind of idiotic bullshit reasoning that results in people like Cass not understanding that you are, in fact, paying for something when you pay interest. Owners own the capital; they carry the risk; they invest, at risk, to create the possibility to produce the thing their outfit produces, which would be far harder or impossible without that investment (which the average worker has no ability to match on their own). The owner also has to handle management since he's ultimately the one who deals with the responsibility of all other aspects of product development, delivery, and sale. He might pay people to do those things or to manage, but at the end of the day since he carries the risk, he has the responsibility to make sure it gets done, and it's mostly his reputation that's on the line.

That is, the owner earns that "surplus value" in a wide variety of ways, even if all he does is assume the risk. He isn't extracting it as an act of theft from the worker. Again, the logic is that labor is a necessary but insufficient condition, and the value Marx called "surplus" goes above the worker's wages by dealing with other necessary conditions until sufficiency is met.

Of course, "surplus value" is yet another resentment concept, aiming to make the worker feel robbed by his employer by systematically making sure he doesn't understand the condition he's in to begin with so he'll be mad not just about the situation but about parts of it he has no reasonable right to be upset about. That surplus anger gets channeled into idiotic pushes for revolution.

And, by the way, that's exactly what postliberal retards like Oren Cass are doing with the same kinds of misunderstanding, targeting largely the same kinds of people in order to get them worked up to achieving Cass's political ambitions for him, even at the threat of their own destruction.

U.S. stocks closed higher Monday, 10.05.26 led by large technology shares. https://t.co/jj0fb4Hh1Q via @YouTube 

U.S. stocks closed higher Monday, led by large technology shares. 

The Nasdaq Composite rose 1.1% to a record close of 27,477. The Samp;P 500 added 0.7% to 7,774, within about 0.3% of its summer high. The Dow gained 0.2% to 51,268. The Russell 2000 rose 0.5% to 2,847. 

That move sat next to a less friendly backdrop. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.31%. Brent crude swung between about $100 and $103 and settled a little above $100. Deal news, including Schneider Electric’s roughly $22.6 billion bid for PTC, supported parts of the tape. Last Friday’s softer-than-expected September jobs report was still in the background. 

September ISM Services PMI printed 54.9, down from 55.4, a 27th straight month of expansion. The prices-paid index rose to 74.0, the highest since July 2022. Activity is still expanding. Services inflation is not cooling with it. 

The rest of the week is lighter on major data, ahead of bank earnings next week. 

Tuesday: the August trade report. Constellation Brands reports after the close. 

Wednesday: minutes of the September 15–16 FOMC meeting, 2:00 p.m. ET. At that meeting, the Committee raised the federal funds target range by a quarter point to 3.75%–4.00%. 

Thursday: weekly jobless claims. PepsiCo reports before the open. 

Friday: preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment. Delta Air Lines reports before the open.

In 1996, a Libyan leader put one billion dollars on the table for Black America. Washington made sure it never reached them.
The offer came during Louis Farrakhan's visit to Tripoli in January 1996. Muammar Gaddafi pledged the money to the Nation of Islam for economic development—Black-owned banks, factories, housing, schools, hospitals. Not a loan.
Not charity with strings. A gift from an African head of state to the descendants of enslaved Africans.
Farrakhan did everything by the book. He applied to the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control for permission to accept the money. The Clinton administration denied it in August 1996. Libya was a state sponsor of terrorism. Sanctions barred the transaction. Case closed.
The Treasury also blocked a separate $250,000 award Gaddafi had given Farrakhan for organizing the Million Man March.
The Nation of Islam was chosen for a reason. Founded in Detroit in 1930, built by Elijah Muhammad, rebuilt by Farrakhan after 1975—it was the only Black American organization with the infrastructure to absorb that kind of capital. They had schools. Businesses. A newspaper. A security force. Hundreds of thousands of members.
Gaddafi saw organization where Washington saw a threat.
Farrakhan fought the decision. He called it a violation of religious freedom and legal rights. He said the money would create joint ventures with Black businesses. He threatened to mobilize across the country. It didn't matter. The Treasury Department had the final word.
Consider the context. The same government that blocked this gift was simultaneously funding death squads in Central America, propping up Mobutu in Zaire, and maintaining close ties with apartheid South Africa. Gaddafi was the enemy. Black economic development, funded by African money, was the threat.
The billion dollars never arrived. Black America never got to find out what it could have built.

@BernieSanders, or should I say @SenSanders , you put a teachers union shirt behind your microphone and asked California to trust it with healthcare.

I'm a teacher. I'll grade it for you.

That shirt says UTLA. United Teachers Los Angeles, the union that runs the show at LAUSD, the second biggest school district in the country. text:
When an injustice occurs, the journalists, historians and archivists document evidence and facts to establish a memory, with an underlying faith: that justice, action and wisdom will follow from it in time. But time in itself offers no such function on its own -- it all comes down to the individual will and effort to make wisdom and justice out of what has occurred. And what if the power imbalance is too great between the victim and the perpetrator? Accountability and enforcement of law require not only will, but also power. The realist in this situation would say: justice can come only if we accrue more power so we no longer remain victims in the future, and so we can enforce laws ourselves that all others have understood and accepted as cherished and supreme for sustained peace. (But power is a double-edged sword: the victim, if powerful and as one-sided as the perpetrator, when in a state of humiliation from the loss of dignity, is in a position with all reasons and emotions in agreement to unleash the very act that was unleashed upon it; after all, the nature of one-sidedness is such that justice for one is injustice for the other; the nature of power is such that it is vital for survival, but also carries in it temptation towards one-sidedness: for ugliness produces only ugliness, and by what justification can the perpetrator be denied the right to act in response from all the rage, hatred, vindictiveness and humiliation that the sight of ugliness has produced and has become all-consuming.)

Documentation of facts and production of history is as equally crucial as accrual of power, and both proceed from an injury; an injury precedes the act of seeking wisdom. Wisdom is earned, which we all hold to be a truism -- but what is actually earned? Injury through injustices from the imbalance of power. Which is to say: wisdom is earned through injustices. The path to wisdom, that is, more consciousness, is paved in blood from the sheer barbaric savagery, the author of which still lurks deep down in us all. Even when wisdom is earned, it is earned for a time, since it has to be earned again, which requires injuries. Where there is power, there can be no universal empathy, and where there is wisdom, there universal empathy can exist.

At least 20 men from Telangana are reported to have been caught in a recruitment network that allegedly took them to Russia after promising civilian jobs. While some have returned, others remain stranded and four are believed to have been deployed to fight for the Russian army against Ukraine.

How did the recruitment happen?

According to complaints from families, agents approached men seeking overseas employment and promised jobs such as cooks, cleaners, gardeners, mechanics, support staff and manual workers.

In one case, Megavath Prakash of Dammannapet in Dharpally mandal paid ₹2.4 lakh to Madhava Rao of Ramadugu for visa and travel expenses. Prakash travelled to Russia and worked for a private company for about four months before it shut down.

Madhava Rao allegedly then offered to arrange another job through Russia-based agents Odde Yellaiah and Telu Krishna, seeking another ₹50,000. Prakash was subsequently taken to Gourav Chaudhary, who allegedly facilitated his recruitment into the Russian Army.

What happened after they reached Russia?

Families said some men were made to undergo military training instead of doing the civilian jobs they had been promised. Accounts shared by returnees described prolonged physical training, inadequate food, insufficient sleep and poor accommodation.

Some men later circulated videos and messages seeking help. One returnee, Kasturi Thirupathi, said, "Because we needed to repay debts back home, we trusted the agents and got cheated."

The men identified include people from Nizamabad, Kamareddy and Sircilla districts. Three of the 16 men identified in a subsequent repatriation effort, Shekar of Banda Lingapur, Rajashekar of Keshapur and Thirupathi of Darpally, have returned home, while 13 were awaiting repatriation.

What action has followed?

Nizamabad police arrested Gourav Chaudhary, 34, a native of Karwar in Uttar Pradesh. Police said he claimed his bank accounts were used by a Russian Army recruitment agency and were verifying whether he acted in connivance with the agency.

Nizamabad MP Dharmapuri Arvind wrote to External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar seeking the repatriation of the 16 men. Arvind also thanked Jaishankar and the Indian embassy for assistance in securing the release of some men.

The Union government has advised Indians to exercise caution over Russian defence-related job offers, avoid unrecognised agents and verify recruitment credentials and employment contracts before travelling to Russia.
